Trump Administration Moves to Terminate Federal Methane Emission Regulations

Policy Shift

President Trump announced the termination of Biden-era regulations targeting methane leaks from oil and gas facilities. Speaking in Lubbock, Texas, the President claimed the move aims to reduce industry costs by an estimated $45 billion and increase domestic oil production by 210 million barrels. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin described the decision as ending a "war on oil and natural gas."

Impact and Background

Previously, the 2024 rule mandated that operators minimize leaking, flaring, and venting of methane—a potent greenhouse gas. Critics, including the Environmental Defense Fund, warn that the rollback could accelerate climate warming and lead to significant resource waste. While industry groups have lobbied for these changes, citing regulatory burden, public health advocates express concern over the loss of oversight on harmful emissions.
